hyps.why: Replacing a removed edge with a 3x3 conv restores connectivity and capacity, a bigger gain than replacing any other op.
Going from none to conv3x3 gives a larger gain than upgrading from an existing parametric or skip op.
Adding a conv to a dead direct edge to the output yields more than swapping ops on an already active edge.
The first edge from the input is key, and re-enabling it with conv3x3 is a big gain over leaving it off.
Replacing none with conv3x3 opens a new feature path, which helps more than replacing another op.
Replacing a conv3x3 with a skip on the direct edge loses capacity, unlike replacing none or pooling.
Removing the direct edge to the output hurts more when edge 5 is also none, since fewer alternate paths remain.
With the direct edge to the output absent, removing edge 5 cuts off a major path to the output.
Removing a conv3x3 edge costs far more than removing a weak op like pooling.
Replacing a useful skip on the direct edge with none costs gradient flow, more than replacing a weak op.
